distinguishing_features: SLIPS liquid-infused micro-textured coating on the tube interior instead of thermal-cycling a stainless wall
Reduces adhesion at the solid-liquid interface via a lubricant liquid layer rather than fracturing deposit bonds by CTE-mismatch thermal stress
Continuous passive anti-fouling during operation instead of periodic duty-cycle shock
Monitored via heat-transfer coefficient / fouling resistance Rf rather than temperature setpoint schedule
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to keep the heat-transfer surface free of adhering protein deposit during operation so that fouling resistance and energy use stay low without scheduled cleaning shutdowns.
parsed.viable_reason: As written the SLIPS coating is physically implausible in a food-contact dairy pasteurizer: the infused lubricant would be sheared away and leach into product, the O-ring containment cannot prevent migration, and no plausible food-safe resaturation within sanitary constraints is demonstrated, so the leak kill-condition and PEG/grease-free operation cannot be met at the stated scale.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: A liquid-infused porous anti-adhesion surface departs from the closest prior art's thermal-shock and setpoint approaches and is not a routine parameter change, so the mechanism itself is not obvious from PRIOR ART 2.
